In [[mathematics]], a '''measure algebra''' is a [[Boolean algebra (structure)|Boolean algebra]] with a countably additive positive [[measure (mathematics)|measure]]. A [[probability measure]] on a [[measure space]] gives a measure algebra on the Boolean algebra of measurable sets modulo [[null set]]s.

==Definition==
A measure algebra is a Boolean algebra <math>B</math> with a measure <math>m</math>, which is a real-valued function on <math>B</math> such that{{sfnp|Jech|2003|p=415|loc=[https://fa.ewi.tudelft.nl/~hart/onderwijs/set_theory/Jech/22-saturated_ideals.pdf chapter 22]}}
*<math>m(0)=0,\ m(1)=1</math>,
*<math>m(x)>0</math> if <math>x \neq 0</math>,
*<math>m(a)\leq m(b)</math> for <math>a \leq b</math>,
*If <math>a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots</math> are pairwise disjoint, then
<math display="block">m{\left(\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_n\right)} = \sum_{n=0}^\infty m(a_n).</math>
